title: Variable-field / magnetic centrifugal filter
alt: Two end barriers give different escape conditions. An inward centrifugal plug can favor light ions. An outward magnetic mirror can favor heavier ions.
mechanism: Rotation and magnetic-mirror barriers give different escape conditions at the two ends.
pros: The two end conditions can send light and heavy fractions to different outlets.
Axial separation can give easier access to the products.
cons: Collisions must supply ions to the loss cones without too much cross-field mixing.
Control of rotation, field geometry, end sheaths, and collection is necessary.
limitations: This diagram shows the end barriers only. It does not calculate the complete field, pitch-angle scattering, loss-cone replenishment, or throughput.

title: Plasma-optical mass separation (POMS)
alt: Energetic ions enter a strong magnetic core with thermionic electron emission. Example paths bend toward separate collection regions.
mechanism: A strong magnetic core changes energetic ion paths. Electron emission and charge-separation fields also change these paths.
pros: The tutorial reports separation experiments with nitrogen, argon, and krypton.
Collection can occur at different radial or axial positions.
cons: The energetic source and nonuniform magnetic field make the apparatus more complex.
Accurate ion-path predictions must include electron emission and self-generated fields.
limitations: This is a conceptual layout. It does not reproduce a POMS experiment or give calculated fields and particle paths.

title: Azimuthal-B / radial-E geometry
alt: An annular cross-section shows an axial conductor, counterclockwise azimuthal B, and outward radial E. Equations give inverse-radius B and logarithmic potential.
mechanism: A central axial current gives Bθ∝1/r. A logarithmic radial potential changes ion orbits in an annular plasma.
pros: Calculations in the tutorial suggest separation with little ion deposition on electrodes.
cons: A large central current and biased plasma electrodes are necessary for this concept.
Prescribed fields alone do not give field penetration, sheath behavior, or collection efficiency.
limitations: This diagram gives ideal geometry and field laws only. The concept differs from POMS and from a magnetic cusp.

title: Radial advection
alt: A local force diagram has E to the right and B out of the page. E-cross-B flow points down. Neutral drag points up.
mechanism: Neutral friction on rotating ions gives radial drift across the magnetic field. Reduced mass and the collision law change each species response.
pros: The mechanism can use rotation already present in a linear plasma.
It helps explain competing radial transport in other separators.
cons: The tutorial gives weak mass dependence for neutral friction.
The calculation inputs must include spatial collision profiles, neutral composition, and density changes with time.
limitations: This local diagram gives force directions only. It does not give measured neutral collision rates, density evolution, or collection fractions.

sources.title: Zweben, Gueroult & Fisch — Plasma mass separation (2018)
Author-hosted tutorial PDF (PPPL)

title: Radial diffusion
alt: Gyroradius squared increases with heavy-ion mass while collision frequency decreases. The two radial diffusion curves coincide in this limit.
mechanism: Random magnetized motion gives radial spread. In the tutorial heavy-on-light Coulomb limit, the leading dependence on test-ion mass cancels.
pros: Cool, dense, collisional plasmas can operate with less auxiliary heat.
cons: The tutorial classical Coulomb limit gives little or no heavy-mass separation.
Fluctuations and other collision channels can have a larger effect than classical diffusion.
limitations: The two curves coincide by design. Each collision operator must have its own coefficients and domain checks.

title: Ion mobility
alt: Two example ion profiles spread and move between biased electrodes. One mean moves faster at equal charge and collision frequency.
mechanism: Electric force and collision drag set a mean drift speed. Thermal diffusion increases the width of each species distribution.
pros: An applied magnetic field is not necessary.
Mass-dependent collision drift can give different species positions.
cons: Diffusion increases the output width and competes with directed flow.
Debye shielding can prevent the assumed field from reaching a neutralized plasma.
Collision frequency depends on the species. Equal ν is an assumption, not a general gas law.
limitations: These example profiles assume equal positive charge and equal collision frequency. They do not reproduce measured output distributions.

title: Differential ionization energy
alt: A Maxwellian electron-energy curve crosses two assumed ionization thresholds. A process diagram separates an ionized product from the remaining neutral atoms.
mechanism: Electron energy changes the ionization rate of each species. Extraction must then separate ions from the remaining neutral atoms.
pros: Different ionization thresholds can give element or molecule selectivity.
Species with low thresholds can be useful targets.
cons: Broad electron distributions and gradual cross-section changes decrease selectivity.
Accurate fraction predictions must include measured cross sections, recombination rates, and extraction history.
limitations: Assumed thresholds and a Maxwellian curve show the mechanism. The diagram does not give measured atomic rates or calculated product purities.

title: Transit time / moving collector
alt: A pulsed source sends equal-energy ions to a moving collector. Ideal arrival markers compare 40 u and 250 u over 10 m at 10 eV.
mechanism: An ion pulse with a narrow energy range spreads in time. Synchronized moving collectors turn arrival-time differences into deposition positions.
pros: Arrival time gives a direct separation coordinate.
Segmented collectors can give mechanical access to deposited fractions.
cons: Energy spread, scattering, and pulse width increase arrival-time spread.
Slits and the pulse duty cycle decrease useful throughput.
A fast moving collector must operate in vacuum.
limitations: Arrival times use the exact ballistic limit at fixed energy. The diagram does not include source broadening, scattering, slit loss, or collector efficiency.

title: Rotating magnetic-field proposal
alt: Four magnetic vectors show successive phases of a transverse rotating field. A list identifies missing electric-field, plasma-response, and transport calculations.
mechanism: The tutorial gives rotating magnetic fields as a separate separation proposal. It refers to external sources for details.
pros: Inference: a time-dependent magnetic drive gives a different control mechanism from static electrode bias.
cons: Section II does not give a complete quantitative field, plasma-response, or collector model.
Accurate predictions must include the induced electric field and current response.
limitations: This diagram shows a rotating-field drive concept only. It does not calculate separator geometry, mass selection, transport rate, or performance.

title: Collisionality-gradient advection
alt: An example collision-frequency gradient connects to diamagnetic flow and species-dependent drift. The diagram identifies missing transport models.
mechanism: A collision-frequency gradient and ion diamagnetic flow can give radial drift. Species mass and energy have an effect on this drift.
pros: The tutorial cites a theoretical method that can give large separation.
cons: The spatial gradients and applicable magnetized collision regime are necessary inputs.
Section II does not give a complete numerical transport model for this method.
limitations: This diagram shows an example collision-frequency gradient only. It does not calculate transport direction, magnitude, collection, or energy cost.

title: Capillary discharge / ion-wind separation
alt: A capillary has heavier-isotope enrichment near the cathode. The diagram lists three possible mechanisms without a numerical enrichment value.
mechanism: The tutorial reports heavier-isotope enrichment near a capillary cathode. It identifies differential ion–neutral friction as the most probable of several proposed explanations.
pros: The tutorial reports experimental isotope enrichment in neon and krypton discharges.
cons: The reported process can be slow. This can prevent high throughput.
Thermal diffusion, differential wall loss, and ion–neutral friction are separate possible mechanisms.
limitations: This diagram shows reported enrichment and possible mechanisms only. It does not calculate isotope flux, discharge behavior, or enrichment factor.
